The story is tightly constructed, with every element introduced in the first half paying off in the second. The narrator's college memories establish Q's seemingly effortless perfection, his compulsive kindness, the narrator's "list of flaws," and the specific motif of the word "solid" (compared to a table). These elements directly set up the climax at the hotel pool ten years later. Q's defining trait—his desire to be gentle and kind—becomes the very flaw that traps him into mishandling the firing/passing over of Dana. In the end, the motifs of the "fourth flaw," the "solid table," and the "shallow/deep end" of the pool all converge to resolve the narrator's decade-long resentment into a moment of empathy and closure.
